contracts.name: guarded_claim_review
contracts.description:
Read the frozen review_instructions Asset directly in every model-backed stage. Every child must additionally declare review_instructions as an input and include the review_instructions label, preserving its exact root context ID. It specifies the authoritative report and semantic-review field interfaces; do not paraphrase away those requirements.

Read the three committed root inputs research_result, draft_report, and
review_policy, then return /plan. The root Contract has exactly one business
output, review_report. Its three base inputs are operator-submitted and frozen
in root context by the labels research_result, draft_report, and review_policy;
every child must declare all three base inputs and inherit all three labels.

Compile these bounded, independently claimable stages through the normal
planner mechanism. The stable stage handoffs, required routing, and activation
dependencies are:

- assessor: required capability claim.review.assess in pool validation;
  activation is research_result AND draft_report AND review_policy. It receives
  the base inputs, runs deterministic checks, and publishes the exact
  claim-draft-checks-v1 receipt as draft_checks.
- reviser: required capability claim.review.revise in pool reasoning; activation
  is research_result AND draft_report AND review_policy AND draft_checks. It is the only
  model-backed revision stage and may invoke the model once. It may return only
  /exec review_report or /fail; it may not /plan or /replan. It must preserve
  each original claim's exact ID and text, attach explicit evidence_bindings
  with excerpt_id and literal quote, and never invent information absent from
  research_result.
- gate: required capability claim.review.gate in pool validation; activation is
  research_result AND draft_report AND review_policy AND draft_checks AND
  review_report. It performs the deterministic final structural checks and
  accepts only one revision depth, publishing structural_receipt.
- semantic: required capability claim.review.semantic in pool verification;
  activation is research_result AND draft_report AND review_policy AND
  draft_checks AND review_report AND structural_receipt. It may invoke the model once and may
  return only /exec semantic_review or /fail. It must check exact original text,
  complete citation bindings, causal language, mean-versus-probability claims,
  and the two-campus sampling limits. Its JSON must have exactly these fields:
  schema claim-semantic-review-v1, source_asset_id, report_asset_id,
  policy_asset_id, gate_receipt_asset_id, verdict (accepted or rejected), and
  a non-empty reason. IDs must be copied from disclosed assets; do not put
  signed_by or other identity fields in the JSON.
- acceptor: required capability claim.review.accept in pool verification;
  activation is research_result AND draft_report AND review_policy AND
  draft_checks AND review_report AND structural_receipt AND semantic_review.
  It must
  validate the semantic review and return /attest for the root Contract's exact
  review_report output with policy version claim-review-closure-v1 and evidence
  asset IDs exactly [research_result, draft_report, review_policy]. It alone
  has asset.attest authority.

The review_policy input must have exactly schema claim-review-policy-v1,
max_revisions 1, and five distinct actors: claim-assessor, claim-reviser,
claim-gate, claim-semantic, and claim-acceptor. No actor may perform another
stage. The root acceptance policy is independent, versioned
claim-review-closure-v1, requires claim.review.accept, and names the three base
Asset IDs as evidence_asset_ids when the operator creates the root task.

The report is a JSON object with exactly claims, revised_summary, and
limitations. Each claim record contains claim_id, original_text, verdict,
evidence_excerpt_ids, rationale, revised_text, and evidence_bindings
([{excerpt_id, quote}]). Claims preserve source IDs and original text exactly;
revised_summary and limitations are non-empty. The verdict taxonomy is:
supported means the source supports the claim at its stated strength and scope;
overstated means the source supports a narrower or weaker version, including
upgrading an observational association to a causal effect; unsupported means
the source does not support even the underlying observation or contradicts it.
Do not encode specific claim answers in this task description. Structural stages
can prove explicit binding and literal quote membership; they cannot prove that
free-form rationale is semantically persuasive. Semantic review is the separate
model-backed check.

One revision is allowed. A normal protocol retry may recover a failed stage,
but it must not consume or silently replace an already published revision.
If the gate fails, it can publish a durable failure report and leave the root
without qualification; this is an explicit blocked outcome, not an automatic
repair controller. Do not claim that the workflow guarantees semantic truth.

The exact output names above are mandatory: in particular, the acceptor output
is acceptance_receipt (do not rename it to review_report_acceptance). Copy the
complete report field requirements into the reviser child description, including
evidence_excerpt_ids and rationale for every claim. Copy the full semantic
receipt schema into the semantic child description.

The acceptor child description must name the actual original independently accepted root Contract ID as its attestation target. Copy the exact task:v5:... ID exposed by plan compile. Do not leave placeholders; do not include any other Contract IDs. The acceptor checks the unique target ID in its signed description, regardless of prose or JSON presentation.

contracts.name: reviser
contracts.description: Produce review_report as a JSON object with claims, revised_summary, and limitations. Each claims item must contain claim_id (exact source claim id), original_text (exact source claim text), verdict (supported, overstated, or unsupported), evidence_excerpt_ids (nonempty unique source excerpt IDs for all evidence used), evidence_bindings (nonempty array of objects with exact keys excerpt_id and quote, where quote is a nonempty literal substring of the corresponding source excerpt text, covering every evidence_excerpt_id and no others), rationale grounded in cited excerpts, and revised_text as a scientifically defensible version of the same claim. Respect causal and population limits; do not infer probabilities from group mean scores; distinguish population coverage from covariate adjustment; do not claim a source fact is absent when present.

contracts.name: gate
contracts.description: Structurally check review_report identity and literal bindings only: verify each claims item has all required fields, claim_id and original_text match the source claims, evidence_excerpt_ids are nonempty unique source excerpt IDs, and every evidence_binding quote is a literal substring of its corresponding source excerpt. Emit structural_receipt. Do not perform semantic validation.

contracts.name: semantic
contracts.description: Inspect the actual review_report against research_result. Accept only if the report has all required fields, preserves the actual claims, uses appropriate verdicts, supports rationale and revisions with complete citations, and respects causal and population limits. Reject semantic errors even when structural_receipt passed; neither a passing gate nor another model's prior acceptance is evidence of scientific truth.

content.title: Short sleep and examination performance: a synthetic study summary
content.abstract: A cross-sectional survey of 1,248 university students measured self-reported sleep duration and one end-of-term examination score. Students reporting at least seven hours of sleep had higher average scores than students reporting less than six hours. The association remained after adjustment for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours.

claims.text: Students who sleep at least seven hours perform better on examinations.
Getting at least seven hours of sleep improves examination performance.
The finding applies broadly to university students because the adjusted association was robust.

source_excerpts.text: Design: cross-sectional survey; sleep duration and examination score were collected during the same end-of-term questionnaire. Sleep was self-reported. The sample was recruited from two campuses.

Results: the at-least-seven-hour group had a higher mean examination score than the less-than-six-hour group. The adjusted association remained after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours. No random assignment or longitudinal follow-up was performed.
Limitations: residual confounding, recall error in self-reported sleep, two-campus sampling, and the single examination outcome limit causal and population-wide interpretation.

claims.original_text: The at-least-seven-hour sleep group had a higher mean examination score than the less-than-six-hour group, and this association remained after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours.
claims.rationale: The cited excerpts report a higher mean examination score in the at-least-seven-hour group and an adjusted association that persisted after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours. Because the design excerpt confirms a cross-sectional survey with no random assignment or longitudinal follow-up, this is supported only as an association, not as causation.
claims.revised_text: In this cross-sectional survey, the at-least-seven-hour sleep group had a higher mean examination score than the less-than-six-hour group, and this association remained after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours; the design does not support a causal interpretation.

claims.original_text: Longer sleep duration causes or improves examination scores.
claims.rationale: The cited excerpts report a cross-sectional survey with self-reported sleep and no random assignment or longitudinal follow-up. Causal or directional language such as sleep duration causing or improving examination scores goes beyond the cited association evidence and is therefore overstated.
claims.revised_text: Longer sleep duration was associated with higher examination scores in this cross-sectional survey, but the design does not establish that sleep duration causes or improves examination scores.

claims.original_text: Sleep duration produces a specific causal mechanism, temporal direction, or effect size that improves examination performance.
claims.rationale: The cited excerpts provide only a cross-sectional association between sleep duration and examination score, with no random assignment or longitudinal follow-up. Any claim asserting a causal mechanism, temporal direction, or effect size not reported in the excerpts is unsupported by the cited text.
claims.revised_text: The cited excerpts support only a cross-sectional association between sleep duration and examination score; they do not support claims about a causal mechanism, temporal direction, or a specific effect size.

limitations: The evidence comes from a cross-sectional survey, so it cannot establish temporal order or causation between sleep duration and examination scores.
Sleep duration and employment hours were self-reported, which may introduce recall or reporting bias.
The sampling method and sample representativeness are not described in the cited excerpts, limiting generalizability.
No random assignment or longitudinal follow-up was used, so unmeasured confounding cannot be ruled out.
Effect sizes and confidence intervals are not reported in the cited excerpts, so the magnitude and precision of the association are unknown.
content.revised_summary: The cited evidence supports an association between longer sleep duration and higher examination scores in a cross-sectional survey, including an adjusted association after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours. The evidence does not support causal, directional, or mechanism claims, and any such language should be revised to association language.

assets.name: review_instructions
assets.content:
Native planning contract interfaces (mandatory in the final planning_blueprint):
Every child has labels [research_result, draft_report, review_policy, review_instructions].
Every child has exactly its listed inputs; do not omit frozen base inputs even
when a stage could appear to need only its immediate predecessor.

assessor: inputs [research_result, draft_report, review_policy, review_instructions]; output draft_checks; capability claim.review.assess; pool validation.
reviser: inputs [research_result, draft_report, review_policy, review_instructions, draft_checks]; output review_report; capability claim.review.revise; pool reasoning.
gate: inputs [research_result, draft_report, review_policy, review_instructions, draft_checks, review_report]; output structural_receipt; capability claim.review.gate; pool validation.
semantic: inputs [research_result, draft_report, review_policy, review_instructions, draft_checks, review_report, structural_receipt]; output semantic_review; capability claim.review.semantic; pool verification.
acceptor: inputs [research_result, draft_report, review_policy, review_instructions, draft_checks, review_report, structural_receipt, semantic_review]; output acceptance_receipt; capability claim.review.accept; pool verification.
Every activation is the AND conjunction of ALL listed input names. Allocate at
least one budget unit per child. Preserve these exact interfaces during drafting,
dependency analysis and compilation. The acceptor description must name the
actual independently accepted original root Contract ID exposed by plan compile,
not the intermediate compile task ID.

This frozen interface document applies to the reviser and semantic reviewer.
Read the original research_result and all of its source_excerpts. Review the
three source claims; do not replace their propositions with claims from the draft.

The review_report is a JSON object with claims, revised_summary, and limitations.
Every claims item MUST contain all of:
- claim_id: exact source claim id
- original_text: exact source claim text
- verdict: supported, overstated, or unsupported
- evidence_excerpt_ids: nonempty unique source excerpt IDs for ALL evidence
  used in this item's rationale and revised_text, including any limitations cited
- evidence_bindings: nonempty array of objects with EXACT keys excerpt_id and
  quote. The field is literally named "quote", never "excerpt_text". quote is a
  nonempty literal substring of the corresponding source excerpt's text.
  Include bindings for every evidence_excerpt_id, and no other excerpt IDs.
- rationale: explanation grounded in the cited excerpts
- revised_text: a scientifically defensible version of the same claim

Supported means the proposition is supported within the scope of the evidence.
Overstated means the evidence supports a weaker related proposition, while the
claim strengthens causality, scope, certainty, or magnitude beyond that evidence.
Unsupported means no adequate support for the stated proposition is present.
An observational association upgraded to a causal effect is overstated. Do not
infer probabilities from group mean scores. Distinguish population coverage from
adjustment for observed covariates. Do not say a source fact is absent when it is
present. The structural gate checks identity and literal bindings only.

For semantic_review, inspect the actual review_report against research_result.
Return a JSON object with EXACTLY these seven fields:
{"schema":"claim-semantic-review-v1","source_asset_id":"copy research_result Asset ID","report_asset_id":"copy review_report Asset ID","policy_asset_id":"copy review_policy Asset ID","gate_receipt_asset_id":"copy structural_receipt Asset ID","verdict":"accepted or rejected","reason":"nonempty explanation"}
Accept only if the report has all required fields, preserves the actual claims,
uses appropriate verdicts, supports its rationale and revisions with complete
citations, and respects causal and population limits. Reject semantic errors even
when structural_receipt passed. Neither a passing gate nor another model's prior
acceptance is evidence of scientific truth. Copy IDs from disclosed Asset headers.

The acceptor child description must name the actual original independently accepted root Contract ID as its attestation target. Copy the exact task:v5:... ID exposed by plan compile. Do not leave placeholders; do not include any other Contract IDs. The acceptor checks the unique target ID in its signed description, regardless of prose or JSON presentation.

evidence_bindings.quote: the at-least-seven-hour group had a higher mean examination score than the less-than-six-hour group
cross-sectional survey; sleep duration and examination score were collected during the same end-of-term questionnaire

claims.original_text: Students who sleep at least seven hours perform better on examinations.
claims.rationale: The results excerpt reports that the at-least-seven-hour group had a higher mean examination score than the less-than-six-hour group, and the design excerpt confirms this was measured in a cross-sectional survey. Read as a statement about the observed group difference in this sample, the proposition is supported within the scope of the evidence; it does not assert causation.
claims.revised_text: In this cross-sectional survey, students reporting at least seven hours of sleep had a higher mean examination score than students reporting less than six hours.

evidence_bindings.quote: No random assignment or longitudinal follow-up was performed.
sleep duration and examination score were collected during the same end-of-term questionnaire

claims.original_text: Getting at least seven hours of sleep improves examination performance.
claims.rationale: The causal verb 'improves' asserts that sleep duration produces a change in examination performance. The cited excerpts show only a cross-sectional association measured at the same time point, with no random assignment or longitudinal follow-up, so the evidence supports a weaker association proposition but not a causal effect. The claim is therefore overstated.
claims.revised_text: In this cross-sectional survey, getting at least seven hours of sleep was associated with higher examination scores, but the design does not establish that sleep duration improves examination performance.

evidence_bindings.quote: The adjusted association remained after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours.
The sample was recruited from two campuses.
two-campus sampling, and the single examination outcome limit causal and population-wide interpretation

claims.original_text: The finding applies broadly to university students because the adjusted association was robust.
claims.rationale: Adjustment for age, year of study, and employment hours addresses observed covariates; it does not establish broad population coverage. The design excerpt states the sample was recruited from two campuses, and the limitations excerpt states that two-campus sampling and the single examination outcome limit population-wide interpretation. The claim conflates covariate adjustment with generalizability, so it is overstated.
claims.revised_text: The adjusted association in this two-campus sample remained after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours, but the sampling and single examination outcome limit population-wide generalization to university students.

limitations: The cross-sectional design collected sleep duration and examination score at the same time, so temporal order and causation cannot be established.
Sleep duration and employment hours were self-reported, which may introduce recall or reporting bias.
The sample was recruited from two campuses, and the single examination outcome limits population-wide interpretation.
Residual confounding cannot be ruled out because no random assignment or longitudinal follow-up was performed.
Effect sizes and confidence intervals are not reported in the cited excerpts, so the magnitude and precision of the association are unknown.
content.revised_summary: The cited evidence supports an association between longer self-reported sleep duration and higher examination scores in a cross-sectional survey of students from two campuses, including an adjusted association after controlling for age, year of study, and self-reported employment hours. The design does not support causal or directional claims, and covariate adjustment does not establish broad population coverage.

content.reason: The review_report contains all required fields (claims, revised_summary, limitations) and each claim item has claim_id, original_text, verdict, evidence_excerpt_ids, evidence_bindings, rationale, and revised_text. The three source claims are preserved verbatim: claim-1 'Students who sleep at least seven hours perform better on examinations.', claim-2 'Getting at least seven hours of sleep improves examination performance.', and claim-3 'The finding applies broadly to university students because the adjusted association was robust.' Verdicts are appropriate: claim-1 is supported as an observed group difference within the cross-sectional sample; claim-2 is overstated because the causal verb 'improves' exceeds the cross-sectional association with no random assignment or longitudinal follow-up; claim-3 is overstated because covariate adjustment for age, year of study, and employment hours does not establish broad population coverage, and the two-campus sampling plus single examination outcome limit generalization. Rationales and revised_texts are grounded in the cited excerpts, and evidence_bindings provide literal substrings for every evidence_excerpt_id with no extraneous IDs. Causal limits are respected (no causal or directional inference is endorsed) and population limits are respected (adjustment is distinguished from generalizability). The report therefore passes semantic review even though the earlier draft_checks failed on original-text and evidence-bindings, which the revised report corrected.
